facts.fact: An OCI tenancy is the root compartment that holds all of an organization's OCI resources; Oracle creates it at sign-up, and users, groups, dynamic groups and federation providers are managed at tenancy level (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/Concepts/overview.htm).

OCI compartments are logical (not physical) groupings for access control, billing and isolation, and subcompartments can form hierarchies six levels deep (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/Content/Identity/Tasks/managingcompartments.htm).
A child OCI compartment inherits policies from its parents (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/Concepts/overview.htm).

IAM resources are global but their master definitions live in the tenancy's home region, so IAM changes must be made there and propagate to other regions (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/Concepts/overview.htm).

A tenancy lives in exactly one realm and can access only regions in it: commercial OC1 (45 commercial regions listed), separate government realms (US Government Cloud, US Defense Cloud, UK Sovereign Cloud, Australia Government and Defence) and dedicated realms; the Generative AI region page also names OC2 (US Gov), OC3 (US DoD), OC4 (UK Gov) and OC19 (EU Sovereign) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/General/Concepts/regions.htm ; https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/model-endpoint-regions.htm).

Trial, Free Tier and Pay As You Go tenancies can subscribe to one region (PAYG can request more through a Subscribed region count limit increase), while Universal Credit tenancies can subscribe to all public commercial regions (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/General/Concepts/regions.htm).

Oracle's OCI billing models are Annual Universal Credits, Monthly Universal Credit (subject to Oracle approval), Universal Credits Pay As You Go, BYOL, Oracle Cloud at Customer and Government Subscriptions (https://docs.oracle.com/get-started/subscriptions-cloud/ocpib/billing-models-offered.html).

The Oracle Cloud Free Tier combines Always Free services with a 30-day trial of US$300 in credits (select countries) (secondary: search summary of the Oracle page) (https://www.oracle.com/cloud/free/).
Signing up for the Oracle Cloud Free Tier requires a credit card, and only one free account is allowed per person (secondary: search summary of the Oracle page) (https://www.oracle.com/cloud/free/).

Oracle Database@AWS is bought through an AWS Marketplace private offer (or a public offer): you request a private offer from the AWS console, Oracle sales negotiates it, you accept it in AWS Marketplace, and onboarding links the AWS account to a new or existing OCI tenancy; Autonomous Database Serverless also has a public offer (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/database-at-aws/oaaws-task-2-request-offer.htm ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/odb/latest/UserGuide/setting-up.html).

Oracle Database@Azure is bought by accepting a private offer in Azure Marketplace under Private Offer Management, then linking or creating an OCI tenancy (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/oracle/oracle-db/onboard-oracle-database).

Oracle Database@AWS onboarding creates the base compartment MulticloudLink_AWS_<YYYYMMDDHHMMSS> and the policies MulticloudLink_AWS_Management, MulticloudLink_AWS_<UNIQUE_ID>_User_Group_Policies, ..._Observability and ..._Tenant_Level, and the docs say not to change or delete them (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/Content/database-at-aws/oaaws-rbac.htm).

Day-one asks for a client engagement (derived from the policy pages): the tenancy OCID, home region and subscribed regions; a user in the right identity domain with that domain's name; membership in a group with a compartment-scoped policy; a sandbox compartment OCID; the dynamic groups or resource-principal policies the agent runtime needs; and VCN, subnet and private endpoint details if public endpoints are blocked (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/iam-policies.htm ; https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/iam-policies.htm).

A client engagement should ask for membership in a group with a compartment-scoped policy such as manage generative-ai-family in the project compartment (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/iam-policies.htm).

A client engagement should ask for a compartment-scoped policy such as manage genai-agent-family in the project compartment (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/iam-policies.htm).
Agent runtimes on OCI need dynamic groups or resource-principal policies, which should be requested on day one (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/iam-policies.htm).

facts.fact: OCI IAM uses identity domains, and each tenancy has a Default identity domain in the root compartment (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/home.htm).

Identity domains provide authentication, SSO and identity lifecycle for OCI, Oracle SaaS and non-Oracle apps, and the domain types you can create depend on your subscription (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/home.htm).

There are six identity domain types: Free (2,000 users, 2 non-Oracle apps), Oracle Apps (1,000,000 users, 2 non-Oracle apps), Oracle Apps Premium (hybrid IAM for Oracle enterprise apps), Premium (full feature set, 5,000 non-Oracle apps, App Gateway for any app), External User (billed per stored user) and External Active User (billed per monthly active user) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/sku/overview.htm).
The Free identity domain type allows 2,000 users and 2 non-Oracle apps (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/sku/overview.htm).
The Oracle Apps identity domain type allows 1,000,000 users and 2 non-Oracle apps (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/sku/overview.htm).
The Premium identity domain type has the full feature set, 5,000 non-Oracle apps and App Gateway for any app (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/sku/overview.htm).

External identity domains have no dynamic groups and no OCI resource management, and the Default domain can't be changed to an External type (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/sku/overview.htm).

Human SSO uses SAML 2.0 federation into an identity domain: you can add SAML 2.0 identity providers and export the domain's SAML metadata (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/home.htm).
OCI identity domains support OIDC for compliant applications (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/home.htm).
Apple became a supported social IdP for OCI identity domains on 2025-11-05 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/identity/).

The seeded sign-on policy Security Policy for OCI Console has rules for MFA for administrators and for all users, and is active by default in new tenancies (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Security/Reference/iam_security_topic-iam_mfa_with_identity_domains.htm).

The Console MFA sign-on policy is not auto-activated if the default sign-on policy was modified or the tenancy is federated (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/Content/Identity/signonpolicies/managingsignonpolicies.htm).

Per OCI user: 3 API signing keys, 2 auth tokens (which do not expire), 2 Customer Secret keys (S3 compatibility), 2 SMTP credentials and 10 OAuth 2.0 client credentials (up to 10 scopes each; the limit can be raised), plus IAM database passwords (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/Content/Identity/Tasks/managingcredentials.htm).

API signing keys are the default SDK and CLI credential, and the SDK config file ~/.oci/config holds user, fingerprint, tenancy, region and key_file (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/Concepts/sdk_authentication_methods.htm).

oci setup config creates the ~/.oci/config API signing key configuration, and oci setup bootstrap does it with a browser-based flow (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/Concepts/sdk_authentication_methods.htm).
Oracle advises using API signing keys only where storing private keys locally is acceptable (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/Concepts/sdk_authentication_methods.htm).
oci session authenticate creates a browser-based session token that expires after 60 minutes by default (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/Concepts/sdk_authentication_methods.htm).
Session token authentication is not supported in the PowerShell or Ruby SDKs (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/Concepts/sdk_authentication_methods.htm).

Auth tokens are Oracle-generated strings for third-party APIs that don't support OCI request signing, for example Swift or OCIR docker login (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/Content/Identity/Tasks/managingcredentials.htm).
OCI auth tokens never expire and can't be chosen or changed (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/Content/Identity/Tasks/managingcredentials.htm).

IAM user OAuth 2.0 client credentials call https://auth.<oci_region>.oraclecloud.com/oauth2/token with grant_type=client_credentials&scope=<audience>-<scope> (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/Content/Identity/Tasks/managingcredentials.htm).
OAuth 2.0 client credential access tokens expire after 3600 seconds, and regenerating the secret invalidates the old one (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/Content/Identity/Tasks/managingcredentials.htm).

Instance principals let compute instances call OCI without stored credentials: OCI issues instance certificates and rotates them several times a day, and instances are granted access through dynamic groups (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/Tasks/callingservicesfrominstances.htm).

Use instance principals with oci ... --auth instance_principal or OCI_CLI_AUTH=instance_principal, Python oci.auth.signers.InstancePrincipalsSecurityTokenSigner(), or Terraform auth = "InstancePrincipal" (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/Tasks/callingservicesfrominstances.htm).
Terraform authenticates as an instance principal with auth = "InstancePrincipal" (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/Tasks/callingservicesfrominstances.htm).
Every instance principal gets compartment_inspect, which can't be revoked (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/Tasks/callingservicesfrominstances.htm).

Resource principals cover non-instance resources (OCI Functions, Generative AI Agents, data ingestion jobs and hosted applications) with a Resource Principal Session Token (RPST), a JWT with res_tenant and res_compartment claims (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Functions/Tasks/functionsaccessingociresources.htm).

OCI Functions authenticate with resource principals; the token is cached for 15 minutes, so policy changes can take that long to apply (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Functions/Tasks/functionsaccessingociresources.htm).

Generative AI Agents and data ingestion jobs authenticate with a Resource Principal Session Token (RPST) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Functions/Tasks/functionsaccessingociresources.htm).

Python uses oci.auth.signers.get_resource_principals_signer() for resource principals, and the env vars are OCI_RESOURCE_PRINCIPAL_RPST and OCI_RESOURCE_PRINCIPAL_PRIVATE_PEM (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Functions/Tasks/functionsaccessingociresources.htm).

facts.fact: OCI Kubernetes Engine workload identity works only on enhanced clusters and only through an OCI SDK (not the Console or API) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/ContEng/Tasks/contenggrantingworkloadaccesstoresources.htm).
OKE Workload Identity cannot be used with dynamic groups (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/ContEng/Tasks/contenggrantingworkloadaccesstoresources.htm).

OKE Workload Identity minimum SDKs: Go v65.32.0, Java v2.93.0 / v3.88.0, Python v2.111.0, .NET v87.3.0, Ruby v2.19.0 (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/ContEng/Tasks/contenggrantingworkloadaccesstoresources.htm).

OKE Workload Identity policy syntax is Allow any-user to <verb> <resource> in <location> where all {request.principal.type = 'workload', request.principal.namespace = '<ns>', request.principal.service_account = '<sa>', request.principal.cluster_id = '<cluster-ocid>'} (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/ContEng/Tasks/contenggrantingworkloadaccesstoresources.htm).

Since 2025-07-17, a JWT from an external IdP can be exchanged for a short-lived User Principal Session Token by POST to https://<domainURL>/oauth2/v1/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange, requested_token_type=urn:oci:token-type:oci-upst, subject_token_type=jwt and public_key (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/api-getstarted/json_web_token_exchange.htm ; https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/identity/identity-jwt-to-upst-token-exchange.htm).

The JWT-to-UPST exchange needs an Identity Propagation Trust (/admin/v1/IdentityPropagationTrusts) plus a confidential app's client credentials (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/api-getstarted/json_web_token_exchange.htm).

With allowImpersonation: true, the UPST is issued for a mapped identity-domain service user, which has no password or API keys, and the original subject is recorded in source_authn_prin (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/api-getstarted/json_web_token_exchange.htm).
IAM released JWT-to-RPST token exchange for workload identity federation on 2026-08-26 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/identity/).

External JWTs (GitHub Actions, Kubernetes, other clouds) are exchanged with requested_token_type=urn:oci:token-type:oci-rpst for ephemeral RPSTs, and claimPropagations copies selected claims, prefixed ext_, into the token for policy evaluation; Oracle frames this as 'zero-footprint access for external workloads and AI agents' (secondary for claim details) (https://blogs.oracle.com/cloud-infrastructure/wif-with-ephemeral-rpst ; https://www.ateam-oracle.com/github-actions-oci-a-guide-to-secure-oidc-token-exchange).

Identity domains support ID-JAG cross-domain token exchange since 2026-10-09: OCI IAM cross-app access exchanges a user ID token for an Identity Assertion JWT Authorization Grant (urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id-jag) and redeems it at a target identity domain (secondary for details) (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/identity/ ; https://blogs.oracle.com/cloud-infrastructure/?p=18791).
OCI ID-JAG cross-app access also accepts ID-JAGs from trusted external IdPs such as Okta (secondary for details) (https://blogs.oracle.com/cloud-infrastructure/?p=18791).
Identity domains added OAuth resource indicators on 2026-10-07 and Client ID Metadata Document support for OAuth clients on 2026-09-23 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/identity/).
Since 2026-04-23, client secrets of Oracle-provisioned applications are no longer visible (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/identity/).

OCI Generative AI API keys are bearer secrets created in the Generative AI service (not IAM signing keys); each key has up to two secrets with their own expirations, shown only once, and can be set active, inactive or revoked with SetApiKeyState (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/api-keys.htm).
The default limit is 100 Generative AI API keys per tenancy (limit name api-key-count) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/api-keys.htm).

Callers send Authorization: Bearer <secret> to https://inference.generativeai.<region>.oci.oraclecloud.com/20231130/actions/v1/chat/completions or .../responses; API keys launched 2026-01-21 (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/api-keys.htm ; https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai/).

Oracle positions Generative AI API keys for testing and early development and recommends OCI IAM signed requests for production, for workloads on OCI Functions or OKE, and to avoid long-lived keys (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).

The oci-genai-auth package provides OciSessionAuth, OciUserPrincipalAuth, OciInstancePrincipalAuth and OciResourcePrincipalAuth as httpx auth for the OpenAI SDK, with api_key="not-used", base URL https://inference.generativeai.<region>.oci.oraclecloud.com/openai/v1 and project=<generativeaiproject OCID> (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).

The OpenAI-compatible OCI Generative AI base URL is https://inference.generativeai.<region>.oci.oraclecloud.com/openai/v1 (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).

facts.fact: Hosted agentic applications accept four inbound auth modes: identity domain bearer tokens (OAuth confidential app with client credentials grant, primary audience and scopes), identity domain browser sessions (OAuth 2.1 Authorization Code with PKCE; GA 2026-10-07), OCI IAM request signatures (2026-07-15), or 'No authentication' (2026-10-21; the app must enforce its own access control) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/governance.htm ; https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/app-authentication.htm).
Identity domain browser-session auth for hosted applications uses OAuth 2.1 Authorization Code with PKCE and went GA on 2026-10-07 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai/).
Hosted applications accept OCI IAM request signatures since 2026-07-15 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai/).
The 'No authentication' mode for hosted applications (2026-10-21) means the app must enforce its own access control (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/app-authentication.htm).

The 'Permissions to Generative AI Resources' page says 'OAuth is the only supported authentication type for agentic tasks', while the newer get-started-agents page documents both API keys and IAM signing for the Responses API, so the OAuth-only statement likely applies to hosted applications (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/access.htm ; https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).

Autonomous Database accepts IAM database tokens once enabled with DBMS_CLOUD_ADMIN.ENABLE_EXTERNAL_AUTHENTICATION(type => 'OCI_IAM') (add force => TRUE if another external auth is enabled) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/enable-iam-authentication.html).

oci iam db-token get fetches an Autonomous Database IAM token (also with --auth security_token or --auth instance_principal) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/iam-access-database.html).

IAM token clients need TCPS, SSL_SERVER_DN_MATCH=ON and TOKEN_AUTH=OCI_TOKEN, and 19c clients must be at least 19.16 (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/iam-access-database.html).

A Generative AI Agents agent acts as a resource principal (request.principal.type='genaiagent', dynamic group resource.type='genaiagent'), and Generative AI API keys appear as request.principal.type='generativeaiapikey' (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/iam-policies.htm).

OCI has no dedicated 'agent identity' principal type: agents use existing principal types, and the IAM release notes for 2025-11 to 2026-11 announce no agent-specific identity type (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/identity/).

OCI IAM policy grammar is Allow <subject> to <verb> <resource-type> in <tenancy | compartment <name>> [where <conditions>], with subjects group, dynamic-group, any-user or any-group and cumulative verbs inspect < read < use < manage (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/Content/Identity/policieshow/Policy_Basics.htm).

Groups outside the Default domain must be domain-qualified in policies: group <identity_domain_name>/<group_name>, or with quotes for dynamic groups, for example dynamic-group '<idcs-domain-name>/<dynamic-group-name>' (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/Content/Identity/policieshow/Policy_Basics.htm ; https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/iam-policies.htm).

The Administrators group policy Allow group Administrators to manage all-resources in tenancy can't be changed or deleted, and the group must always have at least one member (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/Concepts/overview.htm).

IAM deny policies went GA on 2025-11-20 with syntax deny <subject> to <verb> <resource> in <scope> [where ...] (also deny admit and deny endorse), and deny overrides allow (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/identity/deny-policies.htm).
Only the default domain's Administrators group can enable deny policies, and that group is always exempt (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/Content/Identity/policysyntax/denypolicies.htm).

Enabling deny policies creates a root policy restricting who manages deny statements and can't be turned off; the Policy Basics page still says 'Policies only allow access', which predates this feature (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/Content/Identity/policysyntax/denypolicies.htm).

Cross-tenancy access uses paired endorse and admit statements, for example an admit in the resource tenancy granting use database-connections must match an endorse in the user's tenancy (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/iam-access-database-cross-tenancy.html).

Identity domain administrator roles are Identity Domain Administrator (superuser for the domain), Security Administrator, Application Administrator, User Administrator, User Manager, Help Desk Administrator and Audit Administrator, and assigning them inside a domain is separate from OCI IAM policies (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/roles/understand-administrator-roles.htm).

facts.fact: Managing Identity Propagation Trusts needs a token from an app holding the Identity Domain Administrator role (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/api-getstarted/json_web_token_exchange.htm).
Multicloud federation setup names the OCI Identity Domain Administrator as the OCI-side persona (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/database-at-gcp/oagcp-prerequisites.htm).

The Generative AI aggregate resource type is generative-ai-family, granted with allow group <group> to manage generative-ai-family in compartment <compartment> (or in tenancy), and Oracle recommends the full family only for admins or sandbox users (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/iam-policies.htm).

Individual Generative AI resource types are generative-ai-chat, generative-ai-text-embedding, generative-ai-text-rerank, generative-ai-model, generative-ai-imported-model, generative-ai-dedicated-ai-cluster, generative-ai-endpoint, generative-ai-private-endpoint, generative-ai-routing-profile, generative-ai-apikey, generative-ai-project, generative-ai-sandbox, generative-ai-vector-store, generative-ai-vectorstore-connector, generative-ai-vectorstore-file, generative-ai-file, generative-ai-hosted-application, generative-ai-hosted-application-iam, generative-ai-hosted-deployment, generative-ai-container and generative-ai-work-request (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/iam-policies.htm).

generative-ai-response, generative-ai-semantic-store and generative-ai-nl2sql are used in the agents quick start but are not in the generative-ai-family list on the IAM page (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).

Least-privilege inference for a human or app group uses allow group <group> to use generative-ai-chat in compartment <c>, and since 2026-09-03 it can be limited to specific models with where target.model.id in ('<model-1>','<model-2>') (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/add-api-permission.htm ; https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai/).

After creating a Generative AI API key, add a policy such as allow any-user to use generative-ai-family in compartment <c> where ALL {request.principal.type='generativeaiapikey', request.principal.id='<api-key-OCID>'}; narrower forms use generative-ai-chat with target.model.id in (...), or manage generative-ai-response for the Responses API (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/add-api-permission.htm ; https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).

The Generative AI Agents aggregate is genai-agent-family, granted with allow group <genai-agent-administrators> to manage genai-agent-family in compartment <c>, covering genai-agent, genai-agent-knowledge-base, genai-agent-data-source, genai-agent-data-ingestion-job, genai-agent-endpoint, genai-agent-work-request, genai-agent-session and genai-agent-tool (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/iam-policies.htm).
The Generative AI Agents IAM page says genai-agent-family has 'seven' resource types but lists eight (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/iam-policies.htm).

A Generative AI Agents agent needs permission to call models, coarse form: allow any-user to use generative-ai-family in compartment <c> where any {request.principal.type='genaiagent'} (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/iam-policies.htm).

Fine-grained agent model access uses use generative-ai-chat plus read generative-ai-model (plus read generative-ai-endpoint for dedicated endpoints) with the genaiagent condition, or a dynamic group with matching rule ALL {resource.type='genaiagent'} and allow dynamic-group <dg> to use generative-ai-chat in compartment <c> (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/iam-policies.htm).

facts.source: OCI Generative AI Agents data ingestion job
facts.fact: Agents data ingestion reads Object Storage through a resource principal with matching rule ALL {resource.type='genaiagentdataingestionjob'} (optionally with resource.compartment.id) and policy allow dynamic-group <dg> to read objects in compartment <c> (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/iam-policies.htm).

facts.source: OCI Generative AI Agents data ingestion job
facts.fact: For agents data ingestion, bucket, compartment and tag conditions work, but target.object.name or prefix conditions are not supported and can fail ingestion (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/iam-policies.htm).

Agents SQL and database tools read Vault secrets through the agent resource principal: with dynamic group ALL {resource.type='genaiagent'}, grant allow dynamic-group <dg> to read secret-bundle in compartment <c> and allow dynamic-group <dg> to read database-tools-family in compartment <c>, domain-qualifying the group name outside the Default domain (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/iam-policies.htm).

Agent model access, SQL tools and data ingestion can be granted through dynamic groups matching resource.type='genaiagent' or 'genaiagentdataingestionjob' (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/iam-policies.htm).

facts.fact: Hosted agent deployments run as a resource principal with matching rule any {resource.type='generativeaihostedapplication', resource.type='generativeaihostedapplicationiam', resource.type='generativeaihosteddeployment'} and dynamic group policies read repos (OCIR), read vss-family, and optionally read object-family (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/deploy-permissions.htm).

Users get use or manage generative-ai-hosted-application and generativeaihosteddeployment to work with hosted deployments (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/deploy-permissions.htm).

facts.source: OCI Generative AI NL2SQL semantic store
facts.fact: NL2SQL semantic stores run as a resource principal with matching rule all {resource.type='generativeaisemanticstore'}, granted use database-tools-family, read secret-family, read database-family, read autonomous-database-family and use generative-ai-family; admins get manage generative-ai-semantic-store and manage generative-ai-nl2sql (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).

Functions resource principals use dynamic groups with matching rule ALL {resource.type = 'fnfunc', resource.compartment.id = '<ocid>'}, for example allow dynamic-group <dg> to manage objects in compartment <c> where all {target.bucket.name='<bucket>'} (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Functions/Tasks/functionsaccessingociresources.htm).
Free-form tags are not supported in dynamic group matching rules for Functions (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Functions/Tasks/functionsaccessingociresources.htm).

Autonomous Database IAM token access needs a policy such as Allow group DBUsers to use autonomous-database-family in compartment <c>, optionally where target.id = '<adb-ocid>' (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/iam-create-groups-policies.html).

The autonomous-database-family policy is needed for IAM tokens but not for IAM database passwords, and instance and resource principals must be mapped through a dynamic group (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/iam-create-groups-policies.html).

Vault resource types are vaults, keys, key-delegate, hsm-cluster, secrets, secret-versions and secret-bundles; key-delegate lets integrated services use a key without letting the grantee use it directly, and reading secret content needs read secret-bundles (SECRET_BUNDLE_READ) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/Reference/keypolicyreference.htm).
The aggregate secret-family covers secrets, secret-versions and secret-bundles (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/Reference/keypolicyreference.htm).

Oracle Database@AWS uses predefined OCI groups including aws-db-family-administrators, aws-db-family-readers, aws-network-administrators, aws-exa-infra-administrators, aws-exadb-vm-cluster-administrators, aws-exa-cdb-administrators, aws-exa-pdb-administrators, aws-autonomous-vm-cluster-administrators, aws-costmgmt-administrators, aws-metrics-readers and aws-dbmgmt-administrators (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/Content/database-at-aws/oaaws-rbac.htm).

Oracle Database@Azure maps Entra ID groups to Azure roles and replicated OCI groups; Entra ID Administrator (Azure) and Identity Domain Administrator (OCI) do the setup (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/database-at-azure/oaaonboard-task-7.htm ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/oracle/oracle-db/oracle-database-groups-roles).

The Entra ID group odbaa-exa-infra-administrators maps to the Azure role Oracle.Database Exadata Infrastructure Administrator and is replicated to OCI during optional identity federation (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/oracle/oracle-db/oracle-database-groups-roles).

Oracle Database@Google Cloud uses predefined Google Cloud IAM roles such as roles/oracledatabase.exadbVmClusterAdmin and roles/oracledatabase.odbSubnetUser, granted at project level (https://docs.cloud.google.com/oracle/database/docs/iam-overview).
Federation of Oracle Database@Google Cloud to OCI is optional and needs an OCI Identity Domain Administrator (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/database-at-gcp/onboard-federation.htm).

EPM Cloud (OCI Gen 2) is secured by an OCI IAM identity domain named after the Cloud Account Name, and users holding the Identity Domain Administrator role manage EPM users, SSO and role assignment in the OCI Console, with IdP groups (for example Entra ID) able to be synced (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/idcs_create_deployment_usres.html).

OCI IAM policies are written by members of the tenancy Administrators group or by a group allowed to manage policies in the compartment (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/Concepts/overview.htm).

Users, groups, confidential apps and Identity Propagation Trusts are created by an Identity Domain Administrator, or by User Administrator or Application Administrator within their scope (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/roles/understand-administrator-roles.htm).

facts.fact: OCI Generative AI does not retain prompts and responses during inference, and model providers don't use them for training (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/data-handling.htm).
Oracle has contractual Zero Data Retention agreements with Google (Gemini) and xAI (Grok) for OCI Generative AI (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/data-handling.htm).
Oracle has a contractual Zero Data Retention agreement with xAI (Grok) for OCI Generative AI (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/data-handling.htm).

Fine-tuning data is used only for your custom model: it is deleted from the fine-tuning cluster when the job completes, is not shared with third-party providers or used to improve general models, is AES-256 encrypted (optionally also with customer-managed Vault keys), and data in transit uses TLS 1.2 (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/data-handling.htm).

facts.source: OCI Generative AI dedicated AI cluster
facts.fact: Prompts on a dedicated AI cluster are processed by your model on that cluster, not sent to an external provider, and the cluster isn't shared with other customers (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/data-handling.htm).

Cohere, Meta Llama and OpenAI gpt-oss requests stay in OCI, while Gemini and Grok requests go to Google or xAI locations: Gemini in US regions uses Google Americas, Frankfurt uses Google EU, and Osaka or Hyderabad may process globally (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/data-handling.htm ; https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/model-endpoint-regions.htm).

OCI Generative AI Agents does not use knowledge bases or chat data for training, does not retain chat data beyond the session, and stores managed knowledge base data isolated per customer (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/data-handling.htm).

OCI Generative AI regions include us-chicago-1, us-ashburn-1, us-phoenix-1, eu-frankfurt-1, uk-london-1, sa-saopaulo-1, ap-osaka-1, ap-hyderabad-1, me-riyadh-1, me-dubai-1 and me-abudhabi-1, plus US Gov West, US DoD West, UK Gov South and EU Sovereign Central (dedicated only or mostly dedicated); Sydney has no local processing and uses routing profiles, and availability is per model and per mode (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/model-endpoint-regions.htm).

Since 2026-10-20, routing profiles give on-demand access across 30 regions by sending requests to another region, so processing may happen outside the calling region (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai/).
On-demand Generative AI access was added in Jeddah, Jerusalem and Marseille on 2026-10-30 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai/).

OCI Generative AI Agents is available in us-ashburn-1, us-chicago-1, us-phoenix-1, sa-saopaulo-1, eu-frankfurt-1, uk-london-1 and ap-osaka-1 (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/overview.htm).

Enterprise AI Agents (Responses API) launched in Chicago, Ashburn, Phoenix, Frankfurt, London, Osaka, Hyderabad, Sao Paulo and Riyadh (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/generative-ai/enterprise-ai.htm).

Generative AI private endpoints keep model traffic in a VCN and are available for dedicated endpoints, for on-demand mode (2026-01-21) and for imported models (2026-06-30); Zero Trust Packet Routing (ZPR) security attributes can be added (2026-03-27) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/create-private-endpoint.htm ; https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai/).

A Generative AI private endpoint needs a VCN, a private subnet and a DNS prefix, and the default limit is 5 private endpoints per tenancy (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/create-private-endpoint.htm).

A service gateway lets VCN resources in private subnets reach Oracle Services Network services (for example Object Storage) in the same region without an internet or NAT gateway, using the CIDR labels All <region> Services in Oracle Services Network or OCI <region> Object Storage; IAM network sources can restrict bucket access to a specific VCN (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Network/Tasks/servicegateway.htm).

Autonomous Database has three network access options: secure access from everywhere (public, with optional ACL), access from allowed IPs and VCNs only (ACL required), and private endpoint only (VCN with NSG rules) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/network-access-options.html).

Generative AI Guardrails provide content moderation, image moderation (v1.1.0, 2026-05-29), prompt injection detection, PII detection and topic management (v1.2.0); dedicated endpoints use Inform or Block mode (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/guardrails.htm).
On-demand models use the ApplyGuardrails API to apply Guardrails (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/guardrails.htm).

Guardrails versions released are 1.0.0 on 2026-02-26 and 1.0.1 on 2026-05-26, and one can be pinned with guardrailVersionConfig (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/guardrails.htm).
Guardrails topic management and PII detection are English only (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/guardrails.htm).

facts.fact: The OCI Audit service records API calls and keeps logs for 365 days, a tenancy-wide setting; export to Object Storage for longer retention (https://docs.cloud.oracle.com/Content/Audit/Tasks/settingretentionperiod.htm).
OCI Audit records the principal, for example the instance OCID as principalId for instance principals (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/Tasks/callingservicesfrominstances.htm).
No docs page was found that lists Generative AI-specific audit event types (https://docs.cloud.oracle.com/Content/Audit/Tasks/settingretentionperiod.htm).
Fine-tuning training data can be additionally encrypted with customer-managed OCI Vault keys (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/data-handling.htm).

Compliance attestations naming Generative AI include ISO/IEC 42001:2023 (covering OCI Generative AI and Generative AI Agents), Singapore MTCS SS 584 Level 3, the EU Cloud Code of Conduct (Generative AI and Generative AI Agents) and CSA AI STAR; per-service SOC, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, HIPAA and PCI scope comes from Oracle's compliance pages (secondary) (https://blogs.oracle.com/cloud-infrastructure/raising-the-bar-for-trustworthy-ai-at-oracle ; https://www.oracle.com/it/corporate/cloud-compliance/).
Generative AI became available in US Gov West (Phoenix) and the US Defense Cloud on 2026-08-11 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai/).

Annual Universal Credits bill a 12-month pool in advance, debited monthly by usage, with unused credit forfeited; Monthly Universal Credit is a monthly commitment with overage billed in arrears; Universal Credits Pay As You Go has no up-front fee and bills metered usage monthly in arrears at list price or rate card, whichever is lower (https://docs.oracle.com/get-started/subscriptions-cloud/ocpib/billing-models-offered.html).

Generative AI on-demand inference is billed per transaction, where 1 character = 1 transaction (chat = prompt plus response characters; embeddings = input characters), priced per 10,000 transactions; some models may now be priced per token (unverified), so check each model's 'On-Demand Mode' pricing product (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/pay-on-demand.htm ; https://www.oracle.com/cloud/price-list/#genai).

facts.source: OCI Generative AI dedicated AI cluster
facts.fact: Dedicated AI clusters are billed per unit-hour: hosting clusters have a minimum commitment of 744 unit-hours each, fine-tuning has a minimum of 1 unit-hour per job (some models need 2 units), imported models are exempt from the 744-hour minimum, and some models apply a hosting multiplier (for example 2x for Command R+ 08-2024) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/pay-dedicated.htm).

Generative AI Agents agent usage and data ingestion are billed per 10,000 transactions and knowledge base storage per gigabyte-hour; no prices were retrieved because the pricing page returned 403 (secondary: search snippet of the Oracle page) (https://www.oracle.com/artificial-intelligence/generative-ai/agents/pricing).
Oracle Cost Advisor for AI has been in Limited Availability since 2026-10-27 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai/).
The OCI cost estimator has an OCI Generative AI estimator under AI and Machine Learning (https://www.oracle.com/cloud/costestimator.html).

Oracle Database@AWS is billed through the hyperscaler marketplace as an AWS Marketplace private offer (or public offer for some services, such as Autonomous Database on AWS) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/database-at-aws/oaaws-gs-private-offer.htm).
Oracle Database@Azure is billed through Azure Marketplace private offers (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/oracle/oracle-db/onboard-oracle-database).

facts.fact: Enterprise AI Agents in OCI Generative AI went GA on 2026-03-31, adding the OCI Responses API, Projects, hosted Applications, Vector Stores, NL2SQL and an 'OCI Enterprise AI API Key' (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/generative-ai/enterprise-ai.htm).

Enterprise AI Agents is part of OCI Generative AI; Oracle marketing also uses the 'OCI Enterprise AI' brand, while the docs service name is still 'OCI Generative AI' (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/generative-ai/enterprise-ai.htm).
OCI Generative AI exposes the OCI Responses API, added with Enterprise AI Agents GA on 2026-03-31 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/generative-ai/enterprise-ai.htm).

The separate OCI Generative AI Agents service is still documented with its own IAM family genai-agent-family; its latest release note is 'Select Models for Agents' (2026-02-05), and no deprecation is announced (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai-agents/).
GenerateText was deprecated 2025-06-26 and became unavailable 2026-06-26; use the chat and Responses APIs instead (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai/).
SummarizeText was deprecated 2025-06-26 and became unavailable 2026-06-26; use the chat and Responses APIs instead (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai/).
The chat and Responses APIs are the replacement for GenerateText and SummarizeText, which became unavailable 2026-06-26 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai/).
The Cohere command-latest and command-plus-latest aliases were removed on 2026-07-30 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai/).

Managing IDCS federated resources in the OCI Console has been deprecated since 2026-03-18, and the legacy local user DefaultLocalUser has been being retired since 2026-05-18 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/identity/).

Unconfirmed: no official docs.oracle.com page defines the JWT-to-RPST Identity Propagation Trust schema (claimPropagations, ext_ prefix, max claims); those details come from the 2026-08-26 release-note title plus Oracle blog and A-Team posts, and the blog pages returned 403 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/identity/).

Unconfirmed: whether generative-ai-family covers generative-ai-response, generative-ai-semantic-store and generative-ai-nl2sql, which the IAM policies page omits but other pages use (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/iam-policies.htm).

Unconfirmed: current per-token on-demand prices for xAI, OpenAI or Gemini models, since the docs still describe character-based transactions and the oracle.com price list returned 403 (https://www.oracle.com/cloud/price-list/#genai).
Unconfirmed: the Generative AI Agents pricing figures and the exact Universal Credits discount terms were not retrieved (https://www.oracle.com/artificial-intelligence/generative-ai/agents/pricing).

Unconfirmed: the scope of the access page's claim that 'OAuth is the only supported authentication type for agentic tasks', which conflicts with the API key and IAM options on the get-started-agents page (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/access.htm).

Unconfirmed: no list of Generative AI or Agents audit event types and no per-service SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP or HIPAA scope for Generative AI was found (https://www.oracle.com/it/corporate/cloud-compliance/).

Unconfirmed: the private endpoint docs say a model must be on a dedicated AI cluster, while the 2026-01-21 release note adds on-demand private endpoints, so the older docs text may be stale (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/create-private-endpoint.htm).
